subject: Bridgepoint POC: acceptance criteria, timeline & integration steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Vargas <amelia.vargas@bridgepoint.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Apr 2025 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Bridgepoint POC: acceptance criteria, timeline & integration steps

Amelia — thanks again for a great call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up the trial environment.

Key objectives (what Bridgepoint needs to validate):
- Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end latency under 400ms for 512-token prompts under our planned request profile.
- Throughput: sustained throughput of 20 QPS for parallel inference across 3 concurrent workers.
- Quality: model responses must meet your internal benchmark (F1 >= 0.78 on named-entity extraction prompts and coherence score >= 4.2/5 on our shared eval set).
- Security: data residency in us-west1, logs available for 30 days, and no customer PII persisted beyond session context.

Proposed 4-week POC timeline:
1) Week 0 (this week): finalize SOW and access (we need a list of technical contacts, and VPN/VPC connection details if you want private deployment).
2) Week 1: test environment & SDK drop — Redwood provides SDK, example integration, and sample dataset.
3) Week 2: run synthetic load and functional checks; iterate on prompt templates with your SMEs.
4) Week 3: joint evaluation using your eval cases; collect metrics and heuristic feedback.
5) Week 4: wrap-up, business review, next-step recommendations.

Ownership:
- Redwood: provisioning trial infra, SDK + example app, telemetry dashboards, and assistance with initial integration.
- Bridgepoint: providing eval dataset, SME feedback, and network access (if opting for Private).

Technical integration notes (high level):
- SDK: we will provide our TypeScript and Python SDKs (streaming-enabled) and a lightweight server-side example.
- API routes: text generation endpoints (/v1/generate), chat sessions (/v1/chat), embeddings (/v1/embeddings); streaming via server-sent events (SSE) or websocket for low-latency streaming.
- Tool calling: we support structured tool calls via our function-calling schema; we can map Bridgepoint tool specs to Redwood's function interface.

Attachments: I attached a POC template (redwood-poc-template.xlsx) and SDK quick-start (sdk-integration-guide.pdf).

Next steps: please confirm by EOD Monday if the acceptance criteria above align with your success definition, and send the names/emails for the two technical contacts who will participate in the integration work.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0187

Date: Mon, 21 Apr 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bridgepoint POC: acceptance criteria, timeline & integration steps

Thanks Karthik — that summary is very helpful. A few clarifying items from our side:

1) Latency: 400ms p95 is ambitious and desirable — for our initial acceptance we can stretch to 500ms p95 for 512-token prompts, provided throughput and stability are met. Can Redwood surface per-endpoint p95 (not just end-to-end)?
2) Data residency: we need assurance logs are stored in us-west1 and that only aggregated telemetry leaves the VPC for Redwood console. Can you confirm options?
3) Eval dataset: we'll provide a 1k record gold set for NER and 500 conversational prompts for coherence testing by Week 3.

Technical contacts: adding our two engineers — Rajesh Shah (CTO) and myself for orchestration. Rajesh will loop in his infra lead if private networking is required.

We can also shift Week 2 synthetic load to Week 3 if you prefer to validate functionally first.

Best,
Amelia Vargas
Head of Product | Bridgepoint
amelia.vargas@bridgepoint.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Vargas <amelia.vargas@bridgepoint.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Apr 2025 10:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bridgepoint POC: acceptance criteria, timeline & integration steps

Amelia — great, thanks for the flexibility on p95. Confirming items and slight adjustments:

- Acceptance latency: target 400ms p95; acceptance threshold 500ms p95. Redwood will provide per-endpoint p95 and breakdown by network vs. execution.
- Data residency: two options — hosted trial with logs retained in us-west1 and RBAC-limited console access, or Private deployment (VPC peering) where logs never egress the VPC and only aggregated metrics are sent to our control plane. We'll document both in the SOW.
- Timeline tweak: we'll do functional integration in Week 1, then synthetic load in Week 2, and joint eval in Week 3 (more conservative sequencing per your ask).

Action items for Bridgepoint (please):
- Confirm which deployment mode you want for the POC (hosted with us-west1-only logs OR Private via VPC).
- Provide the eval datasets by 2025-04-25 so our infra team can stage experiments by 2025-04-28.
- Share the two technical contacts (I see Rajesh; please share your infra lead email).

Marissa / Dev — can you confirm we can provision the trial (hosted us-west1) by Thursday and attach the SDK bundle to the shared drive?

Thanks — I’ll draft the SOW once we have the deployment choice.

Karthik

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Amelia Vargas <amelia.vargas@bridgepoint.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Apr 2025 14:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bridgepoint POC: acceptance criteria, timeline & integration steps

Amelia / Karthik — quick technical note and what I'll hand off to Rajesh if Bridgepoint chooses hosted trial first:

1) SDK and example app: the SDK supports streaming with two modes — SSE and WebSocket. We recommend WebSocket for sub-200ms incremental token latency; SSE is simpler to integrate for browsers. The example repo includes a small Node server that demonstrates both.
2) API surface: 
   - POST /v1/generate (sync) — accepts prompt, model, max_tokens, temperature, top_p, return_kvcache boolean.
   - POST /v1/chat (session) — session_id, messages[], function_calls optional.
   - POST /v1/embeddings — returns fixed-size vectors for batch inputs.
   - Webhook callbacks for long-running batches (optional).
3) Function/Tool calling: we support a standardized function schema — name, inputs (json-schema), and response bindings. We'll provide mapping examples to Bridgepoint's existing tools (search and internal catalog).
4) Rate limits and quotas for hosted trial: default is 50 RPS with burst to 100 RPS. For your POC we'll temporarily raise the sustained quota to 25 QPS per model to match your throughput success criterion.

Attachments referenced in this thread are uploaded to the Drive link in the metadata. Key files: redwood-poc-template.xlsx (success criteria matrix + test plan) and sdk-integration-guide.pdf (sample code snippets).

If Bridgepoint prefers private deployment, early notice required (3 business days) to arrange VPC peering and IAM.

Happy to hop on a 30-min technical sync with Rajesh and his infra lead — propose Thu 24 Apr 2025 11:00 PT.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Staff Engineer, Integrations | Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.com
